claims.text: The starting catalyst is a near-equiatomic, multi-principal-element alloy with minimal platinum-group-metal content.
Atomic layer deposition at approximately 150 °C can produce a porous CeO2 overlayer thinner than 5 nm on the alloy catalyst.
The CeO2 overlayer will form a stabilized oxygen-buffering interlayer.
The CeO2 overlayer will provide a physical barrier to poisoning species.
The CeO2 overlayer will limit sintering of the underlying catalyst.
The porous CeO2 layer will store and release oxygen during catalytic reactions.
Oxygen storage and release by the CeO2 layer will lower the activation temperature for CO oxidation.
Oxygen storage and release by the CeO2 layer will lower the activation temperature for hydrocarbon oxidation.
The CeO2 layer will protect active sites against poisoning by H2O adsorption.
The CeO2 layer will protect active sites against poisoning by NO adsorption.
The CeO2 layer will mitigate microstructural degradation during long-term aging.
The CeO2-coated catalyst will have lower CO and hydrocarbon light-off temperatures than the unmodified catalyst, with oxidation light-off below 150 °C.
The CeO2-coated catalyst will lose less activity during exposure to H2O and NO than the unmodified catalyst.
The CeO2-coated catalyst will retain activity and structure better than the unmodified catalyst during extended accelerated aging.
Adding the CeO2 overlayer will preserve the catalyst's low platinum-group-metal content.
The predicted improvements will apply during transient low-temperature exhaust operation and accelerated aging intended to represent multi-year vehicle use.
CeO2 has well-documented oxygen-storage and protective properties in catalytic applications.
